short: Age output from tongue ultrasound (M08) is new but unproven: the random frame split shares children between training and validation (M12), so speaker identity can explain the gain.
position: The paper changes one component, the output (M08): a speaker's age regressed by a CNN from single B-mode tongue frames [@xu2021age]. The output is new (none of the 99 paralinguistic studies in the Appendix matches an age-estimation pattern), but the verdict is standard because the evidence does not show that age is decoded. The 80/20 split is random over frames with no grouping by child (§4.1), so frames of the same children almost certainly fall on both sides (inference), and a network that recognises the child returns that child's age; a 0.25 s ultrasound segment identifies 50 speakers with 3.16% error in [concurrent] work [@shandiz2021neural]. Evaluation (M12) is standard but weaker than the best comparable work, which tests held-out children on the same UXTD corpus and finds them well below seen children [@ribeiro2019speaker]. The abstract's "MAE" values are validation MSE in the body (§4.4), and the speech-therapy use is untested. The claim that tongue images carry age information beyond speaker identity (§4.4) is unsupported.
